questions.q: According to the law of demand, other things remaining equal, when the price of a commodity rises, its quantity demanded ______.
questions.e: The law of demand states an inverse relation between price and quantity demanded, ceteris paribus, so the demand curve slopes downwards.

questions.q: The law of supply states that there is a ______ relationship between price and quantity supplied, other things remaining the same.
questions.e: Producers supply more at higher prices, so the supply curve slopes upward from left to right.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Giffen goods.
I. A Giffen good is a luxury good.
II. For a Giffen good, the substitution effect outweighs the negative income effect.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. A Giffen good is an inferior good, and its negative income effect outweighs the substitution effect, so demand rises with price.

questions.q: The price elasticity of demand is defined as ______.
o: change in price divided by change in income
percentage change in income divided by percentage change in quantity
change in supply divided by change in demand
percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price
questions.e: Ed = (% change in quantity demanded) / (% change in price). It measures the responsiveness of demand to price.

questions.q: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that as a consumer consumes more units of a commodity, the ______ from each additional unit falls.
questions.e: Marginal utility is the extra satisfaction from one more unit. It declines as consumption increases, though total utility keeps rising until MU becomes zero.

questions.q: A production function shows the relationship between ______.
o: inputs used and the maximum output obtainable
questions.e: A production function gives the maximum output produced from given quantities of inputs such as labour and capital, for a given technology.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a perfectly competitive market?
o: Free entry and exit of firms
questions.e: Products are homogeneous under perfect competition, not differentiated. The other three are standard features, and firms are price takers.

questions.q: A market with a single seller of a product that has no close substitutes is called ______.
questions.e: Monopoly means one seller with barriers to entry, so the seller has price-making power.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
I. GDP includes the value of intermediate goods.
II. GDP measures the value of output produced by a country's citizens anywhere in the world.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. GDP counts only final goods and services, to avoid double counting, and covers output within the country's territory.

questions.q: A sustained rise in the general price level in an economy is called ______.
questions.e: Inflation is a persistent increase in the general price level, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

questions.q:
Regarding the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), consider the following.
I. Banks hold their CRR as government securities in their own vaults.
II. Banks hold their CRR as cash balances with the RBI.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only II is correct. CRR is kept as cash with the RBI. Holding liquid assets such as government securities with the bank itself is the SLR.

questions.q: The rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities is called the ______.
questions.e: In a repo (repurchase) agreement banks sell securities to the RBI and agree to repurchase them later. The repo rate is the interest charged for this borrowing.

questions.q: Fiscal policy of a government deals with ______.
o: the interest rate set by the central bank
questions.e: Fiscal policy uses taxes, public spending and borrowing to influence the economy. Monetary policy, by the central bank, controls money supply and interest rates.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Reserve Bank of India?
o: Acting as banker to the government
Acting as banker to commercial banks
Regulating money supply and credit in the economy
Accepting deposits from the general public to lend to businesses
questions.e: Accepting public deposits and lending them to businesses is the primary function of commercial banks. The RBI is the banker to the government and to banks, and regulates money and credit.

questions.q: When the price of a good falls from ₹10 to ₹8, its quantity demanded rises from 100 to 120 units. Using the percentage method on the original values, the price elasticity of demand (in magnitude) is ______.
questions.e: Percentage change in quantity = 20/100 = 20%. Percentage change in price = 2/10 = 20%. So the elasticity is 20/20 = 1 (unit elastic).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about perfectly inelastic demand.
I. The price elasticity of demand is zero.
II. The demand curve is a horizontal straight line.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only I is correct. Quantity does not change when price changes, so elasticity is 0 and the demand curve is vertical, not horizontal.

questions.q: If all inputs are doubled and output more than doubles, the production function shows ______.
questions.e: Output rising by a bigger proportion than the inputs is increasing returns to scale. Diminishing marginal returns concern a single variable input.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about cost curves.
I. The marginal cost curve cuts the average cost curve at the minimum point of the average cost curve.
II. When marginal cost is below average cost, average cost falls.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. AC falls while MC is below it, rises when MC is above it, and so MC meets AC at the minimum of AC.

questions.q: If GNP at market price is ₹500 crore and depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) is ₹40 crore, then NNP at market price is ______.
questions.e: NNP = GNP − depreciation = 500 − 40 = 460 crore.

questions.q: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) requires banks to maintain a minimum percentage of their NDTL in ______.
o: liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved securities, held by the bank itself
questions.e: SLR is held by the bank in liquid assets, including government securities, whereas CRR is held as cash with the RBI.

questions.q: The rate at which the central bank borrows surplus funds from commercial banks is called the ______ rate.
questions.e: In a reverse repo the RBI sells securities and borrows money from banks. A higher reverse repo rate draws liquidity out of the banking system.

questions.q: A market with a few large firms whose decisions are interdependent is called an ______.
questions.e: In an oligopoly, each firm must consider rivals' reactions. The kinked demand curve model explains price rigidity here. Oligopsony is a market with few buyers.

questions.q: Which feature is characteristic of monopolistic competition?
o: A single seller of a unique product
A few sellers of identical products
Many sellers of a homogeneous product
questions.e: Monopolistic competition has many firms, free entry and product differentiation (branding), giving each firm some control over its price.

questions.q: In the Indian money supply measures, M1 comprises currency with the public, demand deposits with banks and ______.
questions.e: M1 = currency with the public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with the RBI. Adding time deposits to M1 yields broader measures like M3.

questions.q: If banks must keep a cash reserve ratio of 10% and keep no excess reserves, the simple deposit (money) multiplier is ______.
questions.e: The multiplier is 1/reserve ratio = 1/0.10 = 10. A fresh deposit of ₹100 can support up to ₹1,000 of total deposits.

questions.q: A consumer's income rises from ₹20,000 to ₹24,000 per month and the quantity of a good bought rises from 50 to 65 units. By the percentage method, the income elasticity of demand is ______.
questions.e: Percentage change in quantity = 15/50 = 30%. Percentage change in income = 4,000/20,000 = 20%. Elasticity = 30/20 = 1.5, so the good is a normal luxury-type good (elasticity > 1).

questions.q: Total product for 1 to 5 workers is 10, 24, 36, 44 and 48 units. The law of diminishing marginal returns begins to operate from the ______.
questions.e: Marginal products are 10, 14, 12, 8, 4. MP is highest for the second worker and falls from the third worker onwards.

questions.q: GDP at market price = ₹1,000 crore, net factor income from abroad = −₹30 crore, depreciation = ₹80 crore, indirect taxes = ₹100 crore and subsidies = ₹20 crore. NNP at factor cost (national income) is ______.
questions.e: GNP at MP = 1000 − 30 = 970. NNP at MP = 970 − 80 = 890. NNP at factor cost = 890 − (100 − 20) = 810 crore.

questions.q: A firm's total cost is TC = 100 + 5Q + Q². Its average cost is minimum at an output of ______ units.
questions.e: AC = 100/Q + 5 + Q. Setting dAC/dQ = −100/Q² + 1 = 0 gives Q = 10. Check: MC = 5 + 2Q = 25 equals AC = 10 + 5 + 10 = 25.

questions.q: A monopolist faces demand P = 50 − 2Q and has a constant marginal cost of ₹10. The profit-maximising price is ______.
questions.e: Total revenue = 50Q − 2Q², so MR = 50 − 4Q. Setting MR = MC gives 50 − 4Q = 10, so Q = 10. The price is P = 50 − 2 × 10 = 30.
